subject: Dedicated pool recovery summary + canary rollout plan
messages:
From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@orbital-retail.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Cc: Procurement <procurement@orbital-retail.com>
Date: 2025-06-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Sudden throughput drop on dedicated pool (Orbital prod)

Hi Aditya,

We started seeing a sharp drop in inference throughput on our dedicated pool at ~08:50 PDT this morning. 99th pct latency spiked and a subset of requests failed with timeouts. Impacting checkout recommendation API.

Current customer impact: ~20% of requests returning 5xx / timeouts, elevated latency for the rest. We've routed some traffic to our degraded fallback but that's not sustainable. Can you confirm whether this is a configuration/scale issue on your side or something on our end?

I've attached the short timeline we collected and a small sampling of failed request IDs.

Attachments: orbital_timeline_0618.csv, failed_samples.txt

Thanks,
Alex
Head of Production Engineering
Orbital Retail
From: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@orbital-retail.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2025-06-18T09:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden throughput drop on dedicated pool (Orbital prod)

Alex —

Thanks for the rapid signal and the attachment. We see correlated error spikes from one of the reserved GPU pools in us-west-2. We're triaging now and have pulled logs; engineering is investigating a warmup/eviction pattern that looks like an autoscaler cold-start thrash.

Immediate actions:
- Routing: We pushed an automatic partial routing to a compatible, slightly smaller model to reduce failures (short term).
- Logs: collecting allocator and pod lifecycle traces, will attach a recovery bundle shortly.
- Credits: we'll propose a credit for impact window once we confirm scope.

I'll loop in our ops lead and keep you updated every ~60 minutes until stable.

Apologies for the disruption — we know this touches your checkout flows and prioritize mitigation.

— Aditya
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, diego_fernandez@redwood.ai
Date: 2025-06-18T09:35:00-07:00
Subject: INTERNAL: Orbital dedicated pool - initial triage notes

Folks — quick internal summary and asks. Copying diego for kernel/runtime context.

What we see:
- Time window: 08:48–09:10 PDT spike in evictions and node warmup loops on pool rp-usw2-23.
- Symptoms: allocator lock contention + KV cache misses causing per-request latency to balloon.
- Customer impact: Orbitals call volume ~1.6k qps; dropouts at ~20%.

Immediate mitigation attempted: partial routing to model v2-small (compatible) reduced 5xx rate to ~2% but increased token cost.

Required from eng:
- Diego: pull nvstats, allocator trace, and the autoscaler event log for rp-usw2-23 (08:30–09:30).
- Ops: prepare a canary rollout plan to validate warmup patch (reduce idle evictions, extend warmup window).

Customer comms: I'll send a short update to Alex with planned timeline (postmortem + remediation plan by EOD PDT).

Aditya
From: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@orbital-retail.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, diego_fernandez@redwood.ai
Date: 2025-06-18T10:40:00-07:00
Subject: Update: mitigation in place and next steps

Alex — quick update after the first triage window.

Summary:
- Root cause (high confidence): autoscaler warmup loop + aggressive idle eviction on a subset of reserved nodes in rp-usw2-23 causing repeated cold starts and allocator contention.
- Mitigation applied: temporary partial routing to v2-small (compatible) and increased warmup window on the pool; this brought 5xx rate down from ~20% to ~1.8% and stabilized 99th pct latency.

Next steps / timeline:
- 11:30 PDT: run controlled canary of warmup policy change on adjacent pool (10% of traffic).
- 13:00 PDT: if canary stable, rollout policy to remaining nodes and monitor for 2 hours.
- EOD PDT: postmortem draft and recovery bundle posted to shared drive.

We attached the recovery log bundle for your team to review (recovery_log_bundle_20250618.zip). We're also preparing an action-oriented canary playbook for Orbital to review; attaching draft.

Compensation: we'll propose a credit covering the impacted window once we finalize timeline and scope.

Thanks for working through this with us — we'll confirm the canary result at 11:35.

— Aditya
From: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@orbital-retail.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, diego_fernandez@redwood.ai
Date: 2025-06-19T11:45:00-07:00
Subject: Post-incident summary & recommended canary/playbook (Orbital)

Alex —

Thanks again for patience. Attached is a succinct post-incident summary and an operational canary playbook we've used internally; we tailored it for Orbital to validate the warmup policy change with minimal risk. Highlights:

What happened (TL;DR):
- A confluence of autoscaler warmup tuning and an internal eviction threshold allowed reserved nodes to repeatedly drop into a cold state during a sudden concurrency ramp. Cold starts plus allocator lock contention produced cascading latency spikes and elevated 5xx.

What we changed:
- Warmup window extended from 45s -> 210s for reserved pools with high coldstart sensitivity.
- Eviction hysteresis increased (fewer aggressive evictions during bursts).
- Added a short-term routing policy that prefers model variants with faster warmup characteristics for checkout traffic.

Operational canary (summary):
1) Canary scope: 5–10% of traffic to a sibling pool with extended warmup.
2) Success criteria: 99th latency within baseline + 5xx <= 1% for 30m.
3) Rollback: immediate traffic revert and warmup rollback if 99th latency > baseline + 25% or 5xx > 2%.

Attachments included: recovery_log_bundle_20250618.zip (allocator + autoscaler traces), canary_playbook_Orbital.md (runbook and checklist).

We recommend scheduling a short run-through with your SREs this week so we can walk the steps and tune thresholds specific to your workload. Available windows: Thu 06/20 08:00–10:00 PDT or Fri 06/21 14:00–16:00 PDT — tell me which works and we'll send a calendar invite.

Apologies again for the disruption; we'll also propose commercial credit for the affected window in a separate note through your procurement contact.

Regards,
Aditya Rao
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
Attachments: recovery_log_bundle_20250618.zip (log bundle, 45MB), canary_playbook_Orbital.md (runbook)
